question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & -7 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

If the matrix $A$ above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 4 & -7 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & -1 \\ 4 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((7-\lambda )(3-\lambda )+4) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +25) & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda -5)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=5$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=2.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{2}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=2$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{2})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=5.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{5}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-5I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & -7 & 3\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & -7 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). This implies that we will have $3-2=1$ linearly independent eigenvector corresponding to the current eigenvalue. So, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{5})=1.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is *not* diagonalizable, since 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{2})+\text{dim}({V}_{5})=1+1=2\ne 3.\,\times 
$$
